sample_reviews.marker: Remcos 2.2.2: covert logging, hollowing and UAC bypass; add coverage
reasons: RC4 settings decrypt to a configured remote controller at remcoss.onmypc.org:3765.
Recording keystrokes and clipboard content, destroying browser login/cookie stores, image unmapping and context redirection, and autoelevation registry hijacking establish hostile intent.

Remcos is marketed for remote administration, but covert input recording, browser-store destruction and UAC hijacking together tip this artifact to malicious. No authorization/deployment evidence was supplied.

execution_evidence.resource_recovery: The resource table is physically at 0x19000 although headers map .rsrc to 0x1a000. Walking the intact table locates SETTINGS at raw 0x199a4, length 418. Byte zero gives key length 149; subsequent key and ciphertext decrypt with RC4.
execution_evidence.startup_settings: 0x409146 -> 0x409c5e -> 0x40a0e9 loads SETTINGS; 0x4031b3 implements RC4 KSA; 0x40320d implements PRGA; 0x40329b transforms the resource.
execution_evidence.keylogging: 0x4051dc starts logging worker threads; 0x40538a dispatches key callbacks to key formatting/recording helpers and forwards the hook chain. Clipboard recording helpers are also present.
execution_evidence.browser_destruction: 0x407136 builds UserProfile + Chrome Default Login Data and passes c_str() directly to DeleteFileA at 0x40717c. The 0x4079e7 worker retries multiple browser-store deletion helpers until completion.
execution_evidence.uac: 0x4032e9 gates on OS build, writes HKCU Software\Classes\mscfile\shell\open\command, launches eventvwr.exe using ShellExecuteW, then exits on successful launch.
execution_evidence.hollowing: 0x40f2ef validates a PE, creates a suspended child, reads its image base, conditionally unmaps it, allocates and writes the replacement image and sections, updates PEB/context, then resumes.
execution_evidence.audio: 0x4013c9 opens WinMM input, prepares/adds buffers and starts capture; a separate 0x401814 worker and 0x40193b callback save timestamped WAV data via 0x4016b9.
execution_evidence.analysis_probes: 0x4010f1 calls GetModuleHandleA(SbieDll.dll) and returns presence. 0x4011d2/0x4011e5 call FindWindowA with PROCMON_WINDOW_CLASS/PROCEXPL. 0x401000 and polling threads connect probe results to configurable response logic at 0x401234.
execution_evidence.limits: Malformed section/resource/relocation layout prevents claiming successful runtime startup. Configuration flags gate optional features; rules describe code/API presence, not enabled recording or runtime success. Tria.ge page could not be retrieved; its score was not used as proof.

sample_reviews.marker: UniClipboardEngine: verified upstream source; paired clipboard sync
reasons: Exact SHA-256 match to a fresh GitHub codeload fetch of the claimed UniClipboard/Engine commit; provenance and artifact retained in scratch.
Production dispatch selects current-space usable peer device IDs, applies per-device send/category preferences, and receives only after membership and receive-policy authorization.
XChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypts content with a random nonce and authenticated payload. Network synchronization and local encrypted storage match the declared purpose.

The member scored 1.0 is compatibility/uc-mobile/ios-demo/main.swift: it parses a fixed Base64 golden-vector connection URI, requires an explicit CLI URI for live tests, writes its own generated marker, reads it back, tests a wrong password and tests TLS.

Build scripts generate FFI/link flags, provenance data and test source. with-isolated-source.mjs clones the selected local revision, runs the caller-supplied build command in scratch and removes that scratch directory. CI secret inputs are used in configured build/audit services.
No fetched dependency finding was involved (local, follow=none review). No evidence of a substituted stage or covert destination was found in the inspected execution paths.

execution_evidence.limits: Static source review, not a full application security audit. Member analysis reports flow/embedded-source limitations; important source paths were manually read. No deployment settings or host application were supplied.

sample_reviews.classifier_disagreement: Still flags verified legitimate integration-test source; classifier false positive, no inaccurate rule restored.

sample_reviews.marker: Keyboard hook fixture: inert snippet; retain capability, fix intent
reasons: Byte-identical to existing testdata/taxonomy/input-source/keyboard-hook-log.c outside the submitted batch.

The callback attempts WriteFile of a KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT, which is preserved as capability evidence. The global output handle is never initialized, there is no entrypoint/caller/message pump, and record_keys immediately unhooks.

No concealment, persistence, network sink or working recording destination appears in these complete 394 bytes. This supports a benign incomplete fixture, without claiming every keyboard recorder is benign.

execution_evidence.limits: Callback dataflow manually checked because source flow producer reports a parse limitation. An external caller could turn a modified copy into a recorder, but that context and output-handle initialization are absent here.

sample_reviews.classifier_disagreement: None after correction; source fixture model probability dropped from 0.9428527 to 0.09797133.

rule_review.removed_claim: SetWindowsHookEx(13, ...) plus any nearby WriteFile call did not prove the write contains captured input or that recording is hostile. The unrelated-status-write.c control also demonstrates this unsupported relationship.
rule_review.relocation: The entire original C matcher/scope/proximity is preserved as micro-behaviors/hardware/input/keyboard/hook::numeric-low-level-keyboard-hook-file-write-profile, notable. No filename exception or package exception.
rule_review.consumer_audit: No exact consumers of the removed objective ID existed. Reviewed keyboard-hook-install consumers (including C# recording and window-targeted collection), ancestor selectors, and existing source fixtures. Numeric installation support only adds the supported capability.
rule_review.retained_attack_coverage: All eight prior Remcos hostiles and all six suspicious findings remain. The separate hidden-file C keylogger objective remains hostile and passes a complete hidden recorder control. A broad two-API co-occurrence is no longer an attack conviction.
rule_review.new_coverage: Microphone capture API profile and keylogger/audio/C2 composite; direct Sandboxie and Sysinternals presence probes bind string and IAT operands of the same x86 instruction sequence.
rule_review.fixture_results: Nine controls passed: bound probes, wrong module operand, wrong API operands, wrong window-class operands, missing audio buffer import, existing incomplete C fixture, existing window-hook fixture, complete hidden recorder, unrelated status-file write.
rule_review.model_warning: Installed scanner reported older v18 feature specification; no model or threshold was modified.
